A 57-year-old man developed symptoms of painful stiffness of his back and limbs, muscle cramps, and difficulty in walking in 1984. He first came under a doctor's care in 1984 because of symptoms of his skin and was diagnosed as progressive dermatosclerosis with muscle cramps. He was treated with prednisolone (25 mg daily) and diazepam (30 mg daily) at a hospital, which reduced symptoms to some extent. Despite continued administration of the drugs, however, his symptoms gradually began to worsen, and he was admitted to our hospital in December 1994.

He was treated with prednisolone (25 mg daily) and diazepam (30 mg daily) at a hospital. Double filtration plasma exchange was performed with PVA (Plasmacure, Kuraray, Japan) as the first filter and Evaflux 2A (Kuraray, Japan) as the second. He was treated with an immunoadsorption therapy with a tryptophan-linked PVA (TR-350, Asahi Medical, Japan) by batchwise adsorption method.
Muscular stiffness improved rapidly and painful muscle cramps disappeared after completing the first session of plasma exchange. His symptoms rapidly disappeared again.
He was treated with prednisolone (25 mg daily) and diazepam (30 mg daily) at a hospital. Oral administration of diazepam (4 mg daily) was restarted.
